extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians and advanced graduate students in geometric analysis / Ricci flow
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of analytic/geometric criteria used in the long-time study of the 3D Ricci flow with surgery (canonical neighborhoods, curvature and volume estimates, thick–thin decomposition, persistence of hyperbolic pieces, incompressibility of boundary tori).

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalization of initial data
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions are constructed with normalized initial data (normalization used e.g. so that Rmin(0) is a fixed reference value).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalization enters the evolution/estimates (for instance, deriving lower bounds for Rmin(t) from the differential inequality d/dt Rmin ≥ (2/3) Rmin^2 uses the normalized initial condition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Surgery placement and δ-cutoff rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The surgery procedure performs δ-cutoff surgeries only on δ-necks (each δ-cutoff at a time t has δ = δ(t)), with a maximal cutoff radius h describing the largest surgery scale in a given time interval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surgeries are designed so they do not occur at locations where Rmin(t) is achieved and surgeries do not increase volume; the maximal cutoff radius h for surgeries on [t0/2, t0] is used in several local estimates (if no surgery in [t0/2,t0], take h=0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pinching assumption controlling Rm's negative part
rubrics_metrics.description: The curvature is assumed to satisfy a pinching condition so that the negative part of the curvature operator is controlled by (a function of) the scalar curvature (used in estimates of Rm from scalar curvature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent use: 'by combining with the pinching assumption we have ... Rm ≥ − [f − ...]R ...' This converts scalar curvature bounds into two-tensor bounds on Rm and is repeatedly invoked to pass from scalar to full curvature operator estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rmin differential inequality and lower bound
rubrics_metrics.description: Rmin(t) (the minimum scalar curvature) satisfies d/dt Rmin(t) ≥ (2/3) Rmin(t)^2 on time intervals between surgeries, and hence Rmin(t) has an explicit negative lower bound of order 1/t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to deduce Rmin(t) ≥ −C/(t + const) and to bound terms in volume and area evolution; shows the minimum scalar curvature stays negative but controlled for all t (important for later monotonicity/estimates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Volume monotonicity functional
rubrics_metrics.description: The quantity V(t) (t + 3/2)^{-3/2} is nonincreasing in t (where V(t) is the volume of the solution at time t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This monotonicity is used to extract asymptotic information at large times (e.g., control of volume growth, compactness arguments, and to limit the number/size of hyperbolic pieces via Margulis lemma).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 7.6.1 — scaling limit implies constant sectional curvature
rubrics_metrics.description: If for some r in (0,1) and a sequence t_α → ∞ the rescalings of the solution on parabolic neighborhoods P(x_α,t_α,r√t_α, r^2 t_α) with factor t_α^{-1} converge in C^∞ to a smooth limiting solution defined on P( x̄,1,r, r^2,1], then the limiting solution has constant sectional curvature −1/(4t) at any time t ∈ (−r^2,1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the key local criterion to identify hyperbolic (constant negative curvature) blow-up limits after rescaling around points with appropriate volume/curvature control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local curvature estimate from volume lower bound (Lemma 7.6.2(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given w>0,r>0,ξ>0 there is T(w,r,ξ,ε) such that if at time t0 ≥ T the geodesic ball B_{t0}(x0, r√t0) has volume at least w r^3 t0 (and an appropriate lower sectional-curvature bound), then at x0 and time t0 one has |2t R_{ij} + g_{ij}| < ξ (i.e. the metric is close to a hyperbolic metric at that scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This local quantitative criterion converts a scale-invariant volume lower bound (and mild curvature lower bound) at large times into closeness-to-hyperbolic estimates; assertions (ii) and (iii) extend the control to larger spatial balls and forward parabolic neighborhoods respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical neighborhood assumption for high curvature points
rubrics_metrics.description: Points with sufficiently large scalar curvature have canonical ε-neck or ε-cap neighborhoods; such canonical neighborhoods have controlled sizes σ with C1(ε) R^{-1/2} ≤ σ ≤ C2(ε) R^{-1/2}, curvature bounds comparable to R, and small volume (Vol ≤ ε σ^3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This structural assumption is used to identify where surgeries may be performed (on necks), to construct thin regions, and to obtain contradictions when assumed alternatives would violate these canonical shapes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thick–thin decomposition criteria (Theorem 7.6.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any w>0 and small ε>0 there exists ρ(w,ε)>0 such that for large times t the manifold M_t decomposes as M_thin ∪ M_thick satisfying: (a) x∈M_thin iff there exists r with 0< r√t < ρ√t such that Rm ≥ −(r√t)^{-2} on B_t(x, r√t) and Vol_t(B_t(x,r√t)) < w(r√t)^3; (b) x∈M_thick iff |2t R_{ij} + g_{ij}| < ξ on B_t(x, ρ√t) and Vol_t(B_t(x, ρ√t)) ≥ (1/10) w (ρ√t)^3. Moreover, scaling limits of thick points converge to complete hyperbolic manifolds of finite volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the principal scale-wise criterion separating regions that are metrically collapsing (thin) from those approximating hyperbolic geometry (thick); the quantitative inequalities (curvature lower bounds, small-volume condition for thin; closeness to hyperbolic and volume lower bound for thick) are exact hypotheses/conclusions used in the decomposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-time behavior trichotomy (Theorem 7.6.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a solution with normalized, compact, orientable, irreducible initial data and appropriate δ(t), r(t) surgery rules, one of three long-time alternatives holds: (i) for all large t the manifold is entirely thin (M_t = M_thin); (ii) there exists a sequence t_α→∞ so that scaled essential-component metrics t_α^{-1} g_{ij}(t_α) converge to a hyperbolic metric on the original compact manifold M; or (iii) there are finitely many complete noncompact finite-volume hyperbolic manifolds H_1,...,H_m and truncations K_l such that for large t the essential component contains diffeomorphic images of the K_l with t^{-1} g_{ij}(t) arbitrarily close to the hyperbolic metrics on each K_l, and the complement lies in the thin part, with the boundary tori incompressible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives the main classification/result for long-time behavior and provides precise geometric/topological criteria (hyperbolic convergence or decomposition into hyperbolic pieces + thin complement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence criterion for hyperbolic pieces (harmonic map continuation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A limit hyperbolic piece H_a persists if, for suitable choices of truncation area a, Sobolev/Holder indices and small parameters (l0, q0, δ0, ε0), one can find harmonic diffeomorphisms F_α from the truncated hyperbolic piece (H_a) into (M_{t_α}, t_α^{-1} g_{ij}(t_α)) converging in C^k; these harmonic maps can be continued forward in time while staying close in C^k, showing the hyperbolic piece persists in the evolving manifold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical matching/compactness/implicit-function arguments (Lemmas 5.3.7, 5.3.8, and elliptic regularity) provide the exact quantitative smallness conditions ensuring persistence; used to produce 'persistent hyperbolic pieces' in alternative (iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incompressibility of boundary tori via least-area disk argument
rubrics_metrics.description: If a boundary torus of a persistent hyperbolic piece failed to inject π1 into the complement, Dehn's Lemma gives a curve bounding an embedded least-area disk D in the complement; the normalized area A(t) of such a minimal disk then decreases at a rate ≥ const/t (derived from the metric evolution and boundary term estimates), leading to contradiction (non-integrable decay), hence the boundary tori must be incompressible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses existence of least-area embedded disks (Meeks–Yau / Meeks–Simon–Yau), evolution ∂_t g_{ij} and Gauss–Bonnet type estimates for area/length terms, and the fact surgeries do not affect the hyperbolic pieces to reach the contradiction; this is the exact geometric/topological criterion ensuring incompressibility in alternative (iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Surgeries do not affect negative-scalar-curvature regions or hyperbolic collars
rubrics_metrics.description: Surgeries are performed on δ-necks in ε-horns at very high scalar curvature, so regions where scalar curvature is negative and hyperbolic pieces (cusplike collars) are unaﬀected by surgeries; in particular, minimal disks and boundary tori for hyperbolic pieces lie outside surgery regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This property is used to justify applying the same continuous/elliptic arguments (least-area disk, harmonic map continuation) across surgery times and to ensure area/volume estimates remain valid despite the discrete surgery events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale-invariant curvature and volume control via parabolic neighborhood estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a local volume lower bound at scale r√t0 one can find constants τ,K (from Theorem 7.5.2 / 7.5.1) so that the solution is defined and satisfies curvature upper bounds R ≤ K (r√t0)^{-2} on the corresponding parabolic neighborhood P(x0,t0,r√t0, τ (r√t0)^2). Combined with the pinching assumption this gives two-sided curvature control |Rm| ≤ K' (r√t0)^{-2}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the standard criterion used to obtain precompactness for rescalings (Hamilton compactness) and to apply Lemma 7.6.1; explicit constants (τ,K,K') depend on the volume parameter w and ε and are used to produce the T(·) in Lemma 7.6.2.
